title: Trump's Hormuz Mess Was Still Showing Up at the Gas Pump
description_short: Trump's Hormuz Mess Was Still Showing Up at the Gas Pump
description_medium: Even after the Strait of Hormuz reopened to commercial vessels, traffic fears and regional instability threatened to keep gasoline prices elevated for consumers already hit by the war's oil shock. It showed how quickly Trump's war posture translated into ordinary economic pain, with everyone else left to absorb the bill for his swagger.

title: Trump: Roy Cohn stars in Joseph McCarthy's investigation, invents McCarthyism
description_short: Trump: Roy Cohn stars in Joseph McCarthy's investigation, invents McCarthyism
description_medium: In 1953, Senator Joseph McCarthy appointed Roy Cohn chief counsel to the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations. PBS says McCarthy relied on Cohn for contacts, information, ideas and political advice during investigations associated with the Red Scare. The appointment is documented, but the supplied accounts do not show that Cohn alone invented McCarthyism or connect the event to Donald Trump.
description_long: Senator Joseph McCarthy appointed Roy Cohn chief counsel to the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations in 1953. PBS’s account says McCarthy relied heavily on Cohn for contacts, information, ideas and political advice. The committee’s investigations became a prominent part of the Red Scare, when allegations of communist influence in government and public life drew national attention. Before the appointment, Cohn gained notice for his role in the prosecution of Julius and Ethel Rosenberg; the supplied timeline says FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover referred him for the counsel post. Cohn held an influential legal and political role in McCarthy’s investigations, but the sources do not establish that he invented the broader phenomenon called McCarthyism. They also do not connect this 1953 appointment to Donald Trump. PBS confirms the year but not the timeline’s precise January 2 date. The evidence supports Cohn’s appointment and role, not the title’s claim of sole authorship or a Trump connection.

title: Trump: Czech Intelligence: Donald Trump is tax exempt until 2007
description_short: Trump: Czech Intelligence: Donald Trump is tax exempt until 2007
description_medium: A 1977 Czechoslovak intelligence informant described Donald Trump’s businesses as “completely tax-exempt for the next 30 years,” according to a file later reported by The Guardian. The article attributes the statement to the informant; it does not verify Trump’s tax status or explain the basis. A separate file reportedly summarized his prenuptial agreement with Ivana.
description_long: The Guardian reported that Czechoslovak intelligence monitored Donald Trump and his then-wife Ivana during the 1970s and 1980s. A 1977 informant report, attributed to a source using the cover name “Lubos,” described Trump’s businesses as receiving state commissions and said they were “completely tax-exempt for the next 30 years.” The article presents that as the informant’s claim, not a verified account of Trump’s tax status, and the file did not explain the basis for it. A separate intelligence file reportedly summarized a prenuptial agreement under which Trump would pay Ivana $1 million if the marriage ended. Later reporting about Trump’s tax returns described a $916 million loss on his 1995 return that could have reduced his income-tax liability for up to 18 years; that is distinct from the informant’s statement. The file documents what the informant told Czechoslovak authorities, not a tax determination or complete account of the couple’s finances. The title’s tax-status claim should therefore remain attributed to the informant.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Czech Intelligence: Donald Trump is tax exempt until 2007
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Czech Intelligence: Donald Trump is tax exempt until 2007

notes: The tax-exempt statement is an informant's claim in a Czechoslovak intelligence file, not verified tax status; the Guardian account says the file does not explain the basis. Proposed correction: attribute the statement to the informant and avoid asserting that Trump was actually tax-exempt.

title: Trump: Carl Icahn destroys industry giants, helps debilitate the Midwest
description_short: Trump: Carl Icahn destroys industry giants, helps debilitate the Midwest
description_medium: The Washington Post reported that Trans World Airlines asked the Transportation Department in May 1985 to block Carl Icahn’s hostile takeover bid, arguing that he lacked airline-management experience and might cut routes or sell assets. The supplied reporting does not establish the later takeover outcome or effects on St. Louis and the Midwest. It also does not document a role for Donald Trump.
